evidence.title: Remove unused AllowedHosts, ProductCodes and the TrimStrings stub
evidence.why: Nothing outside its own test calls `AllowedHosts` or `ProductCodes`, and `config/hosts.php` only feeds the unused singleton. `TrimStrings` is never registered, and its `$except` repeats the framework parent's defaults, so deleting it changes nothing. If host allow-listing is planned, wire it (for example `trustHosts()`) instead. The skeleton `tests/Unit/ExampleTest.php` asserts `true`. `tests/Feature/ExampleTest.php` is a useful smoke test of `/`, so it stays.

evidence.title: Cast Offer columns, keep accepted out of fillable, use L13 attributes
evidence.why: `accepted` is not cast, so the raw column comes back (a string like `banana` was stored and the resource hides it with `(bool)`), and `accepted` is fillable, so any mass write can flip it. `User` already uses `#[Fillable]`/`#[Hidden]`, so `Offer` and `Order` are the odd ones on a 13.x app. Keep `scopeAccepted()` as it is: a `#[Scope] accepted()` method would collide with the `accepted` attribute wherever the column isn't loaded (as in /offers/titles before F-003). The resource now omits `accepted` when unloaded instead of guessing `false`; the `$attributes` default (the column's default) keeps it present on a freshly created offer, which the old `(bool)` fallback was hiding.

evidence.title: Aggregate revenue per country in SQL instead of loading every order
evidence.why: Every request hydrates the whole `orders` table into PHP to add integers, so cost and memory grow with the order count. `sum`/`group by` returns one row per country. `(int)` keeps integer output on MySQL, where `sum()` returns a decimal string.
evidence.suggested:
return Order::query()
            ->selectRaw('country, sum(total_cents) as total')
            ->groupBy('country')
            ->orderBy('country')
            ->pluck('total', 'country')
            ->map(fn (mixed $total): int => (int) $total)
            ->all();

evidence.title: Validate offers input in FormRequests and persist only validated data
evidence.why: `store` spreads `$request->all()` into `create()`, so a client sets `accepted` (and any other fillable key) and unvalidated values are stored: `accepted="banana"` returned 201 and was saved as the string `banana`. `price_cents` has no upper bound (an out-of-range value reaches the column; SQLite accepted 5,000,000,000 with a 201), and `?accepted=maybe` or `?accepted=0` is silently read as 'no filter'. The rewrite also tightens JSON integers with `integer:strict`. `accepted=0` now returns not-accepted offers instead of all offers, which is a behaviour change to confirm.

evidence.title: Remove or wire the unused AllowedHosts and ProductCodes classes
evidence.why: Only their own unit tests use them (no controller, middleware or job calls either class), and `config/hosts.php` carries a placeholder host list. Dead code tests nothing the app does. Confirm they are not for a pending feature.
evidence.suggested:
Delete app/Support/AllowedHosts.php, app/Support/ProductCodes.php, config/hosts.php, tests/Unit/AllowedHostsTest.php, tests/Unit/ProductCodesTest.php, and the singleton binding plus its import in AppServiceProvider::register().
If host allow-listing is planned, use $middleware->trustHosts() instead.

evidence.why: The loop builds a `$seen` array by hand. `uniqueStrict()` keeps the strict `in_array(..., true)` comparison (plain `unique()` would merge '0' and '00'), and `array_values(...->all())` keeps the declared `list<string>` return without a temp variable.
